# EXOLINE — Phase 4: Galaxy Expansion and Final Civilization
> This is the execution manual for one month of solo development. Treat the master briefing as the global architecture contract and this file as the active delivery schedule.
**Duration:** one month.
**Phase exit condition:** A player can expand across all 60 systems, reach Civilization Level 10, and activate the Continuity Core.
**Source-aligned scope:** 60-system galaxy map; interstellar expansion; civilization levels; AI advisors; ML forecasting; final infrastructure parts; Continuity Core; victory activation; endless mode; performance optimization.
## 0. Month Operating Philosophy
- UI and simulation are developed together.
- Every week ends with a runnable browser demo.
- Every feature gets an explicit data contract before visual polish.
- Do not add a feature merely because it appears in a later phase.
- Use placeholder art where necessary, but never placeholder behavior for the core mechanic.
- Prefer deterministic systems first; tune realism after the end-to-end loop works.
- Keep every major state inspectable in the UI.
- At the end of the month, create a tagged build.
## 1. Phase Goals
### Week 1: Galaxy map and interstellar progression
The week must close with a visible demo and a tested integration point.
### Week 2: Civilization levels and system autonomy
The week must close with a visible demo and a tested integration point.
### Week 3: AI/ML advisor integration and final infrastructure
The week must close with a visible demo and a tested integration point.
### Week 4: Continuity Core, endless mode, performance, and final release
The week must close with a visible demo and a tested integration point.
## 2. UI Deliverables
- Persistent application shell.
- Top navigation with active location and simulation status.
- Global alert and event area.
- Context inspector.
- Primary page for the phase's core feature.
- Empty, loading, error, blocked, and success states.
- Keyboard-accessible controls for important interactions.
- Numerical formatting helpers with units.
- Simulation time controls.
- Developer-facing diagnostics during development builds.
## 3. Architecture Deliverables
- Schema files for all new mutable state.
- Rust/WASM simulation module or boundary stub appropriate to the phase.
- Worker message definitions.
- TypeScript read-model adapters.
- React components.
- PixiJS layer when the phase includes visual simulation.
- Unit and integration tests.
- Persistence integration.
- Logging.

## 6. Weekly Integration Rule
### Week 1 gate
- The browser build starts from a clean environment.
- The phase's primary feature is accessible from the main navigation.
- The current state is visible without developer tools.
- At least one success path is testable end-to-end.
- At least one failure path is understandable.
- The save/load path does not lose the phase's newly introduced state.
- The demo can be recorded in under five minutes.

## Day 01 — Galaxy map and interstellar progression
**Month:** 4 | **Week:** 1
**Daily objective:** finish a user-visible slice while advancing the underlying contract.
**Required evidence:** browser screenshot, automated test result, and a short changelog entry.
- Create or update the contract/schema before implementation.
- Implement the smallest deterministic simulation path.
- Expose the result through the Worker protocol.
- Build the corresponding React view.
- Add a PixiJS scene only when spatial rendering is part of the feature.
- Add a test fixture.
- Exercise the path manually in the browser.
- Record what remains deliberately unimplemented.
- Day 1: keep galaxy-scale progress visible from the civilization overview.
- Never make an AI recommendation the only route to progress.
**UI checkpoint:** confirm loading, ready, success, blocked, and error states where the day's feature can enter them.
**Engineering checkpoint:** keep simulation work outside the render loop and keep Worker messaging explicit.
**Test checkpoint:** add or update at least one deterministic test covering the changed behavior.
**End-of-day definition of done:** the project starts cleanly, the feature is demonstrable, and unfinished work is recorded.

## 7. End-of-Month Hardening
- Run unit tests.
- Run integration tests.
- Run end-to-end happy path.
- Run end-to-end failure path.
- Run save/load round-trip.
- Run deterministic replay or golden test.
- Check console for uncaught exceptions.
- Check browser performance on the target machine.
- Check that the UI can explain the core mechanic without external narration.
- Tag the release.
- Archive the demo build.
- Write a known-limitations note.
- Do not start the next phase until the exit condition is reproducible.
## 8. Phase Demo Script
1. Open galaxy view.
2. Travel from Sol to an unlocked system.
3. Establish a colony.
4. Inspect system self-sufficiency.
5. Use at least one AI advisory feature.
6. Progress civilization level.
7. Build final infrastructure.
8. Construct the Continuity Core.
9. Activate it.
10. Observe endless mode.
11. Run performance checks.
12. Show final game overview.
